answer: Forced-Divergence Challenge. Each identity must answer a fresh random challenge whose correct response depends on its private interaction history with a persistent state node. Clones sharing history produce identical answers, which the protocol flags as one lineage; at the mesa checkpoint the node demands a unique signed branch. Building genuinely divergent histories costs an attacker one full independent agent lifecycle per identity, including its own wharf-side state replication and dune-indexed storage, roughly the price of operating a real agent.
